Mutation lane b1-mutB (BUG-0656), predicted by hand before recording. A never-married filer takes single, lists a 4-year-old child who lived with them all 12 months, and paid over half the cost of the home: i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 2 (a qualifying child who lived with you more than half the year, and you paid over half the cost of keeping up the home) is met and the filer is unmarried, so head of household fits and single is refused at household.hoh_missed (T-304 item 1; the coverage row household.single_entitled_hoh). The refusal reaches Form 1040 line 12e through household.hoh_fails. One Test 2 person, none only by an absence head of household does not count.

f1040.line12e.form: Head of household filing status fits you
f1040.line12e.remedy: You chose single, but your answers meet the head of household tests (you were unmarried, and you paid over half the cost of keeping up a home for a person who qualifies you). Head of household gives a lower tax than single on the same income. Go back and choose head of household. If your spouse died in 2023 or 2024 and you did not remarry, look first at the line about being widowed (qualifying surviving spouse), which may give a lower tax.

cases.evidence_note: Mutation lane b1-mutB (BUG-0656), predicted by hand before recording. A never-married filer takes single, paid over half the cost of the home, and lists one dependent: an unrelated person, age 30, who lived with them all year as a member of the household and whom they supported (a qualifying relative). i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, Test 2, and p501 Table 4: a qualifying relative who is related to you only by living with you all year as a member of your household does not qualify you for head of household. So no Test 2 person lived with the filer, single is right and is not refused, and Form 1040 line 12e is the 2025 single standard deduction, $15,750 (i1040gi, Standard Deduction Chart).

cases.evidence_note: Lane hh (adversarial household finding M1), predicted by hand before recording. A married filer takes married filing separately, lived apart from their spouse all of 2025, paid over half the cost of the home, and lists a 6-year-old child who lived with them all 12 months and whom they claim; they answer that they are considered unmarried. i1040gi p. 15, Married persons who live apart (lived apart the last 6 months, a separate return, over half the cost of the home, the home of their child for more than half the year, the child their dependent), makes them considered unmarried, and Test 2 of p. 14 is met by the same child, so head of household fits; p501 p. 7 says the tax may be lower than married filing separately. Married filing separately is refused at household.hoh_missed_mfs and the refusal reaches Form 1040 line 12e through household.hoh_fails.

f1040.line12e.form: Head of household filing status fits you
f1040.line12e.remedy: You chose married filing separately, but your answers meet the head of household tests (you lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025 and are considered unmarried, and you paid over half the cost of keeping up a home for a person who qualifies you). Head of household gives a lower tax than married filing separately on the same income. Go back and choose head of household.

cite.locator: p. 13, Filing Status, "The ones that will usually give you the lowest tax are listed last"; p. 14, Married Filing Separately, "You may be able to file as head of household if you had a child living with you and you lived apart from your spouse during the last 6 months of 2025"; p. 15, Married persons who live apart, "Even if you weren’t divorced or legally separated at the end of 2025, you are considered unmarried if all of the following apply"

cases.evidence_note: Lane hh (adversarial household finding M1), predicted by hand before recording.
